messages.subject: interpreting getP() output
parts:
Hello All,

I'm trying to make sure I understand what getP is outputting. 

It gives me a matrix with 5 columns (1 for each distance bin, if I've got this right) and 363 rows (one for each transect). I am not using any covariates to explain detection, so the numbers in each column are the same for all rows.

Is the number in column 1 the detection probability for the first distance bin? and the number in column 2 the detection probability for the second bin, etc? The numbers decline so that is what I'm guessing but I wanted to make sure i was understanding the output correctly. 


In other words: 
If my first column has 0.65 and my collaborator wants to report our detection probability 'on the line' is it correct to say that detection on the line is 65%?

I'm using gdistsamp if that makes a difference. most recent version of unmarked  on cran. 

Thanks as always for your input,

Auriel

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] interpreting getP() output
parts:
Hi Auriel,

For gdistsamp, getP returns the interval-specific detection probability, conditional on an individual begin available for detection. As with most other distance sampling methods (and if the individual is available for detection), detection probability is assumed to be 1 when distance=0. However, detection probability for the first interval will be less than 1 because it is the average detection probability of individuals in that interval. 

Hope that helps.

Richard
